title: Executive Boardroom Reservation Maximization
real_world_story: A corporate headquarters has one executive boardroom equipped with telepresence video walls. N project teams have submitted reservation requests for today. Team i requests the boardroom from start minute s_i to finish minute f_i. Only one meeting can occupy the boardroom at any point in time. If meeting A finishes at minute T, meeting B may start at minute T. Facilities management aims to accommodate the maximum number of distinct project meetings in the boardroom.
problem_statement: Given N meeting requests with start time s_i and finish time f_i (where s_i < f_i), find the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings that can be scheduled in the boardroom.
task: Compute the maximum number of mutually compatible meetings that can be hosted in the boardroom.
input_format:
The first line contains a single integer N, the number of meeting requests.
The next N lines each contain two space-separated integers s_i and f_i, representing the start and finish times.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings that can be scheduled.

examples.explanation: Sorted by finish time: [1, 3], [2, 5], [4, 7], [6, 9], [8, 10]. Selecting [1, 3] leaves [4, 7] and [8, 10] compatible. Total scheduled = 3 meetings.
Meeting [10, 20] and meeting [20, 30] do not overlap interior time (one finishes at 20, the next starts at 20). Selecting both yields 2 non-overlapping meetings.

real_world_takeaway: Greedy activity selection based on earliest finish time provably achieves the optimal packing of non-overlapping intervals in a single shared resource.
